value: small eyes covered by the maxillopalatine bones; open orbit absent (closed)
method: skull osteology from micro-CT of one specimen (RAM 0020)
conditions: Nine specimens, all female, 112-209 mm total length, collected 14 July 2015 near Peria, Wayanad, Kerala, India; the skull was described from one micro-CT scanned specimen (RAM 0020, 198 mm preserved total length)

source.authors: Palakkool SR, Gower DJ, Kotharambath R
source.title: Osteology of the caecilian Gegeneophis carnosus (Beddome, 1870) (Amphibia: Gymnophiona: Grandisoniidae) from the Western Ghats of peninsular India

quote: The eyes are small and covered by maxillopalatines, and so orbits are absent (closed).
note: The sentence does not name the species; the whole paper describes G. carnosus (title). The Abstract states the same ('The eye is covered by the maxillopalatine, and an (open) orbit is absent.'). No eye diameter is given. Family and order as printed in the title. value: none (eyes absent, ocular structures completely degenerated)
conditions: Four snails (holotype NCUDX251201, shell length 2.05 mm, and three paratypes, one an empty shell) collected August 2025 in a cave in Hongta District, Yuxi City, Yunnan, China, 2062 m altitude, with a fishing net of mesh under 1.5 mm

source.authors: He Y-M, Xiang H-Q, Yang J-M, Zheng H, Yang S-Z, Zhou Y-F, Zheng J
source.title: A new eyeless species in Erhaiidae (Gastropoda, Truncatelloidea) from a cave in Yuxi City, Yunnan, China

where: Systematics, Erhaia dijiang sp. nov., Description
quote: All individuals examined to date absence of eyes, with complete degeneration of ocular structures.
note: Quote reproduces the printed grammar. The sentence sits under the heading for the new species and does not repeat its name. The Abstract also says the species is characterized by the absence of eyes. A co-occurring unnamed Pomatiopsidae snail is said to have normal eyes. Order not filed (Truncatelloidea is a superfamily). Licence: page prints CC BY 4.0 and Crossref lists CC BY 4.0 (vor).

value: eyes extremely reduced: corneas extremely reduced, eyes hard to find on the ocular mound, two deepened spots of retinal pigment
method: morphological description of preserved cave specimens
conditions: Three type specimens (male holotype, female paratype, male paratype) from Cueva Doña Otilia, Malargüe, Mendoza, Argentina, about 350 m from the entrance, collected 20 August 2006 and 4 April 2012; fixed specimens

source.title: A relictual troglomorphic harvestman discovered in a volcanic cave of western Argentina: Otilioleptes marcelae, new genus, new species, and Otilioleptidae, new family (Arachnida, Opiliones, Gonyleptoidea)

where: Taxonomic treatment, Otilioleptes marcelae sp. nov., Description
quote: Ocular mound low and unarmed, covered by small granules; eyes are hard to find among granulation since corneas are extremely reduced (in all specimens, two spots of retinal pigment deepened, probably because of retraction of internal tissues during fixation).
note: The author attributes the deepened pigment spots to retraction of tissue during fixation. The sentence does not repeat the species name; it sits under the species heading. Family named in the same paper (new family); order as printed in the title. Licence: page and Crossref list CC BY 4.0 (vor).

method: morphometrics of preserved cave-collected specimens (Mann-Whitney U test columns also printed)
conditions: N = 15 (holotype plus 14 paratypes) from a completely dark cave in Hongguo Town, Panzhou City, Guizhou, China, collected 2021; Table 4 compares this species with S. angularis, S. bicornutus, S. rhinocerous, S. zhenfengensis and S. hyalinus (N = 1); all units mm; each species has a Range cell then a Mean +/- SD cell

source.authors: Xu C, Luo T, Zhou J-J, Wu L, Zhao X-R, Yang H-F, Xiao N, Zhou J
source.title: Sinocyclocheilus longicornus (Cypriniformes, Cyprinidae), a new species of microphthalmic hypogean fish from Guizhou, Southwest China

note: new trait: eye_diameter_mm (no eye-size key exists). S. longicornus is the first range and mean cell pair: mean 1.1 +/- 0.5 mm, range 0 to 1.6 mm (a range starting at 0 means some specimens have no measurable eye). Column assignment follows the printed header order. The ED abbreviation is explained in the paper's methods. The Description says reduced eyes are present in the upper half of the head with eye diameter less than interorbital distance (IOD 5.5-8.6 mm).
